note: Preserved candidates from an interrupted Deep Scan. Locations refer to the pre-patch snapshot; this is not a clean final report.

findings.title: A same-repository PR author can expose the Codex Security API key by editing the workflow
findings.summary: A collaborator who can push a branch in the repository can modify the `pull_request` workflow in that branch and open or update a PR. The fork-only gate passes for that branch, and the resulting workflow run makes the reusable `CODEX_SECURITY_API_KEY` available before a trusted reviewer approves the workflow change.
findings.remediation: Run the credentialed scan from a workflow definition that PR authors cannot modify before execution. Use a protected environment with required reviewer approval, or a carefully constrained base-branch-controlled `pull_request_target`/external dispatcher that checks out the PR only as data and invokes only the pinned scanner—never repository scripts. Keep fork and same-repository contributor trust policies explicit, and scope the API key to the minimum project and budget.

assertions: A collaborator who can push a repository branch satisfies `head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.
Editing the workflow in the PR can redirect the secret before the change is merged to the protected branch.
counterEvidence: The referenced checkout and scanner actions are pinned, repository scripts are not executed before scanning, and checkout does not persist its Git credential.
The current documentation says the workflow, repository secret, and remote protection settings had not yet been activated.
limitations: The review could not inspect live GitHub Actions permissions, protected-environment approval rules, or the OpenAI API key's project scope and budget.
validation.summary: The PR event admits same-repository heads, the only explicit trust check rejects forks, and the admitted job receives a reusable repository secret. Review and CODEOWNER requirements described for merge do not occur before the PR workflow run.

findings.title: Repeated PR updates can run overlapping hour-long security scans
findings.summary: A same-repository PR author can push commits repeatedly and start a new credentialed security scan for every `synchronize` event. Because the concurrency group contains the per-run `github.run_id`, no two runs share a group and `cancel-in-progress` never cancels the superseded scans.
findings.remediation: Use a stable concurrency key for the logical PR, for example `codex-security-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}`, and keep `cancel-in-progress: true`. Do not include `github.run_id` or the head SHA. Add enforceable API-project spend/rate limits and ensure the required-review job accepts results only from the current PR SHA.

assertions: `github.run_id` is different for each workflow run.
`cancel-in-progress` only cancels an earlier run in the same concurrency group.
Each pushed PR commit can create a new group and invoke a full credentialed scan.
counterEvidence: Fork PRs do not pass the scan job's repository-equality gate.
GitHub-hosted runner concurrency, organization Actions policies, and OpenAI project budgets/rate limits may constrain the realized impact.
limitations: No live workflow runs were triggered, and the review did not have access to repository or API-project rate-limit settings.
validation.method: Static GitHub Actions trigger and concurrency trace
validation.summary: A PR author controls the frequency of `synchronize` events. The group key differs for every resulting run, so older hour-long API scans remain eligible to continue.
